sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Cell-surface ELISA (anti-HA, OD492nm) confirmed surface trafficking; CRE-SeAP cAMP reporter confirmed Gs signaling activity — both preserved relative to mock-transfected control.
sites.rationale: No paper in the ledger names a specific residue for the N-terminal HA tag; however, for a signal-peptide-bearing receptor the tag must be inserted after SP cleavage (residue 25, G) to avoid being cleaved off — the mature N-terminus (V26) is the sole extracellular N-terminus, making this the only possible junction. Python confirmed seq[24]='G' and seq[25]='V', consistent with the landmarks (SP 1–25, extracellular 26–570). The large extracellular N-terminal domain (545 residues to TM1) provides ample steric room. L5 from the same paper demonstrates that this HA-tagged WT construct reaches the cell surface and retains Gs-coupled signaling. PMC4982218 (L4/L5): Full-length human ADGRD1 was N-terminally tagged with an HA epitope and C-terminally tagged with FLAG, transfected into cells, and assessed for cell-surface expression by ELISA and for CRE-SeAP signaling activity. The WT HA/FLAG-tagged construct served as the reference baseline (surface expression 0.70 ± 0.11 OD492nm; signaling 786,125 ± 85,787 counts).

sources.claim: The human ADGRD1 was N-terminally tagged with a haemagglutinin (HA) epitope and C-terminally tagged with a FLAG epitope based on [ 22 ]. nsSNPs were generated through site-directed mutagenesis strategy.

literature_notes: All C-terminal tags in the ledger (FLAG in L4, GFP in L6, BioID2 in L7/L8/L9, Twin-Strep in L10/L11) are placed at the protein's C-terminus (after residue 874). The topology landmarks place residues 806–874 in the intracellular compartment; these tags therefore face the cytoplasm and are recorded in other_positions. L6 (mouse Gpr133 N-terminal 3×FLAG knock-in) corroborates the N-terminal extracellular tag site as an ortholog but L4 is the direct human ADGRD1 evidence and is used as the primary clip. No ledger line reports a tag insertion in any of the short extracellular loops (ECL1 623–631, ECL2 696–711, ECL3 781–784) or anywhere else in the large ectodomain at a named residue, so no additional internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal FLAG tag on full-length human ADGRD1; the C-terminus (residues 806–874) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface-accessible site.
C-terminal BioID2 fusion on GPR133 (same protein); confirmed functional by cAMP HTRF assay, but the C-terminus is intracellular — not a surface tag site.
C-terminal Twin-Strep-tag on GPR133 (WT and H543R cleavage-deficient); used for co-purification, but the C-terminus is intracellular — not a surface tag site.
